incidents.victim: Organizations running PHP worldwide, including U.S. federal civilian agencies
incidents.vector: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed 'PHP2Shell') affect every PHP build since version 5.4 and are exploitable via a plain HTTP request before any application code runs.
incidents.impact: CISA added both CVEs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirming exploitation attempts, giving federal civilian agencies until Oct. 29 to patch; Censys found more than 10 million of 42 million exposed PHP instances patched so far, but millions remain on end-of-life branches that will not receive fixes.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health System
incidents.vector: A ransomware gang calling itself 'BYOD' breached the health system's network; the specific initial access method has not been disclosed.
incidents.impact: The hospital diverted ambulances for about two hours, suspended outpatient surgeries and appointments, and canceled medical school classes; the attackers claim to have compromised 36,000 machines and stolen data on students, patients and employees. Federal law enforcement has been notified.

incidents.vector: A threat actor used a LiteLLM master key — exposed in a May leak tied to an experimental 'LiteLLM Agent Platform' project — to gain GitHub access and insert an infostealer into a LiteLLM package version released last week.
incidents.impact: The compromised release distributed credential-harvesting malware to LiteLLM users before the issue was identified and the leaked master key traced to its source.

incidents.vector: Threat actors compromised customer accounts as part of a broader, industry-wide campaign targeting AI infrastructure providers.
incidents.impact: Customer credentials and AI API keys were stolen; the stolen access to AI infrastructure was reportedly resold on underground forums.

incidents.victim: Dahua surveillance camera operators in Ukraine, including government and military users
incidents.vector: Attackers exploit Dahua's Easy4IP cloud remote-access feature via guessable device serial numbers, weak or default passwords, and outdated firmware, including CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045.
incidents.impact: Hackers gained unauthorized access to internet-connected cameras and video recorders, changed device settings and created unauthorized user accounts; researchers warn malicious accounts can survive password changes and factory resets without a firmware update.

incidents.vector: Intruders gained access to internal business systems via a learning management system and a customer relationship management platform.
incidents.impact: Internal business systems were compromised; the company says it found no evidence attackers pivoted to its public customer clouds.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached an internal platform via an unnamed CRM tool used by business partners to sell energy contracts.
incidents.impact: ENGIE is notifying affected customers of its French gas supply business about the security breach.

incidents.vector: An 'infinite mint' smart-contract exploit allowed attackers to create unauthorized tokens.
incidents.impact: Attackers created and stole $2.7 million worth of tokens.

incidents.victim: Enterprise GitHub users (dozens of organizations, including private repositories)
incidents.vector: Attackers use GitHub tokens stolen via infostealer malware and prior supply-chain leaks to plant a disguised 'sync-check' GitHub Actions workflow that prints repository secrets to a workflow log, then exfiltrates and deletes the log via the GitHub API.
incidents.impact: More than 13,500 malicious branches were created across over 850 compromised GitHub accounts; stolen cloud credentials from affected organizations were used to enumerate AWS Secrets Manager at roughly a dozen companies.

incidents.vector: A flaw in eMudhra's April 2025 key-generation ceremony produced critically weak private keys (as little as 3-8 bits of entropy instead of 384) for eight intermediate certificate authority certificates, making the keys trivially recoverable.
incidents.impact: Six compromised TLS and two code-signing intermediate certificates could have been used to impersonate websites or forge signed code; Chrome, Mozilla, Apple and Microsoft revoked or blocked the affected certificates, and Go patched its standard library to reject them. No malicious exploitation has been observed yet.

incidents.victim: Organizations across education, financial services, healthcare, government and other sectors (global)
incidents.vector: Ransomware operators exploit the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication-bypass flaw CVE-2026-0257 for initial VPN access, then move laterally via RDP and SMB and pivot into vCenter/ESXi infrastructure to disable security controls and steal domain credentials.
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations have been breached since June 2026; attackers have disabled hypervisor security controls, performed offline domain-credential theft from virtual disks, and deployed ransomware.

incidents.vector: A suspected Chinese-speaking actor (tracked by Recorded Future as TAG-217) used the AI-assisted penetration-testing framework ARTEX to opportunistically test for and exploit weaknesses across multiple institutions.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to at least 68,000 people was exposed across seven financial institutions; one breach exposed an outsourced developer's data, while another resulted in theft of customer data.

incidents.vector: State-directed North Korean IT workers use stolen identities, paid facilitators and 'laptop farms' to obtain remote technology jobs at U.S. companies while concealing their location and nationality.
incidents.impact: Revenue funds North Korea's weapons programs; the scheme poses an insider-threat and intellectual-property-theft risk to employers, and facilitators have reportedly been threatened and extorted.

incidents.vector: An unidentified third party misused the company's member information retrieval API to extract customer records in bulk.
incidents.impact: More than 22.5 million customer records were compromised, including email addresses, passwords, names, addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and employment information.

incidents.victim: IDCFrontier (Japanese cloud provider) and its downstream customers
incidents.vector: Not disclosed; the incident affected IDCFrontier's cloud hosting infrastructure.
incidents.impact: The ransomware attack disrupted services for 495 companies and local governments that rely on IDCFrontier's cloud platform.

incidents.victim: A water utility, telecommunications provider, regional government body and university in Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries across Europe, Africa and Latin America
incidents.vector: The group exploited on-premises Microsoft SharePoint flaws, including the 2025 ToolShell vulnerabilities, to plant a web shell, then used a tool to disable security software across roughly 40 hosts in about two hours before deploying Warlock ransomware via the domain's SYSVOL share.
incidents.impact: At least four organizations outside the United States were compromised in the two months before Oct. 1, 2026, disrupting operations at a water utility and a telecommunications provider among the victims.
